title: IAM and service accounts
description: Sample quiz: authenticating workloads, choosing roles, and handling service account keys.

questions.question: What is the recommended way for an application running on Cloud Run to authenticate to Google Cloud APIs?

choices.A: Attach a user-managed service account to the service and use Application Default Credentials
choices.B: Embed a service account key file in the container image
choices.D: Make the target APIs publicly accessible

questions.justification: An attached service account provides short-lived credentials automatically through the metadata server, and client libraries pick them up with Application Default Credentials. Embedded keys can leak, personal credentials tie the app to one person, and public APIs remove access control.

questions.question: Which type of IAM role best supports least privilege in most cases?

choices.B: Predefined roles scoped to a specific service
choices.C: The Owner role on the project

questions.justification: Predefined roles grant only the permissions needed for a service or task. Basic roles are far broader. Use a custom role only when no predefined role fits, because you then maintain the permission list yourself.

questions.question: Which are risks of long-lived service account keys? (Select all that apply)

choices.A: They can leak if committed to source control
choices.B: They do not expire by default
choices.C: Google rotates them automatically every 90 days
choices.D: They only work from the VM where they were created
choices.E: Anyone holding the key can authenticate as the service account from anywhere

questions.justification: A downloaded key is a bearer credential: it can leak (A), it stays valid until you delete it (B), and it works from any location (E). Google does not rotate user-managed keys for you (C), and keys are not tied to a machine (D).

questions.question: A service account in project A must create resources in project B. What is the best approach?

choices.A: Grant that service account an appropriate role on project B
choices.B: Download a key for the service account and store it in project B
choices.C: Create an identical service account in project B and share its password
choices.D: Move project B into project A

questions.justification: A service account is a principal that you can grant roles on any project. Binding a role in project B lets it act there without sharing keys. Service accounts have no passwords, and projects cannot be nested inside each other.
